notes.name: Pia Quist
Joel Vasquez
notes.body:
Removed the guard and took your version. After codegen the field resolves without
the `in` check, so the compile-time guarantee is back. Kept the Array.isArray
normalization.

notes.name: Pia Quist
notes.body:
@bfinch, a QA heads-up on how to reach these cards, since the gating is narrower than it looks and "no card appeared" is not by itself a bug report.

The panel only renders when **all three** hold:

1. the record has at least one reporter with a `temperatureFactors` leaf,
2. the workspace flag `highlights.temperature` is on for the tenant, and
3. the summary job has run at least once since the record was last edited.

Condition 3 is the one that trips people up: on a freshly seeded record the job is queued but has not landed, so the panel is legitimately empty for a minute or two. Re-open the record rather than filing on the first empty render.

Seed script for a record that satisfies all three:

```sh
bun run scripts/seed.ts --preset temperature-highlights --tenant demo
```

If it is still empty after the job lands, that is worth a ticket, and the job log is the first thing to attach.

notes.name: Joel Vasquez
notes.body:
Added the seed preset to the MR description so it does not get lost in the thread.
Also filed a follow-up to surface "summary pending" in the empty state instead of
rendering nothing, which is the actual paper cut here.

notes.name: Pia Quist
notes.body:
Naming nit that is worth doing now rather than later: `factor` is used for two different things in this file. In `buildFactorRow` it means one row of the panel, and in `temperatureFactor` it means the scalar the row is computed from. Two readers already asked me which one `factors.length` counts.

Suggest `rows` for the first and `factors` for the second, which also makes the guard read the way it behaves:

```ts
const rows = panelTemperatureFactors(panel).map(buildFactorRow);
if (rows.length === 0) return null;
```

Not blocking, but it is a two-minute rename while the file is already open.

notes.name: Joel Vasquez
notes.body:
Renamed. `rows` for the rendered rows, `factors` for the scalars, and the empty
check now reads off `rows`.

notes.name: Pia Quist
Joel Vasquez
notes.body:
Good catch, the sort really was unpinned. Added the reverse-order case and it fails
without the sort, which is what I wanted to see.

notes.name: Pia Quist
notes.body:
Last one, and it is only a question: the panel fetches its own copy of the record through `usePanelRecord` even though the parent already has it in context. On a page with six panels that is six identical requests, deduped by the cache today but only because the cache key happens to match.

Is there a reason not to read it from context here? If the panel is meant to be usable standalone, say so in a comment and I will drop it.

notes.name: Joel Vasquez
notes.body:
Standalone use is real (the harness renders this panel with no parent), so I kept the
hook and added a comment saying why. The cache key is asserted in the hook's own
test now, so the dedupe is not accidental any more.
